chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: Typhoid fever in Los Angeles
summary: He fell ill with typhoid in Los Angeles at nineteen; Orpheum booking agents cared for him in a hotel across from the Biltmore, and he lost his hair.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Went out to the West Coast, we played Seattle, and we played down the Coast, down to Los Angeles. And then I got sick in Los Angeles, I got typhoid fever.
So they had to leave me there.

Yeah, I got it on my way down. So I was sick -- I was very sick. And I remember I stayed at a little hotel, San Carlos, or something or other, across from the Biltmore. So, the booking agents of the Orpheum time looked after me and they came every day and they got doctors and they took care of me.
That was pretty good. I don't know that a booking agent would do that today, to -- do you?
I don't know that a booking agent would

do that today, to a member of a group, do you think they would? Well, I think they left liked me and yes, they had to. And this Jack Tiboo in Chicago, made the calls, and with the connection in Chicago ---
-- they looked out. I couldn't be moved.
And, oh gosh, I was sick. And then --
That's not funny typh -- now typhoid's back for hearing too.
I know that. I lost my hair, it came out and everything.
When I came back in it was thin, yeah. I was really sick.

It's the first time I had ever been sick. I didn't know what being sick was like before. I came through it all right. But the interesting thing about being sick that year, was that now, let's see it was '26, then. 1926. And I walked over in the park, which is in Los Angeles, that park. I forget the name of it, it's right downtown. I used to sit in the sun. And I could walk -- just make it across the street.
